title: "Nested Subqueries"
number-depth: 2
format: 
    html:
        code-fold: false
---

```{=html}
<p>A <b>subquery</b> is a <code>select-from-where</code> block placed <i>inside</i> another query. SQL allows subqueries in three places, and what the subquery must return depends on where it sits.</p>
<div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>where</b><span>a set (or a single value) to test against</span></div><div class="box"><b>from</b><span>any relation, used like a table</span></div><div class="box"><b>select</b><span>exactly one value: a scalar</span></div></div>
<p class="flow-caption">Examples on this page use the course datasets (university, flis, lis) from the Datasets section. Every output shown is exactly what PostgreSQL returns.</p>
```

## Subqueries in the `where` Clause

```{=html}
<p>Used to test <b>set membership</b> (<code>in</code>), <b>set comparison</b> (<code>some</code> / <code>all</code>) and <b>set cardinality</b> (<code>exists</code> / <code>unique</code>).</p>
```

### Set Membership: `in` / `not in`

```{=html}
<p><code>A in (subquery)</code> is true if the value of <code>A</code> appears in the subquery result. <code>not in</code> is true if it does not.</p>
<p><i>Example:</i> Find courses offered in Fall 2009 that were <b>also</b> offered in Spring 2008.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
select distinct course_id
from section
where semester = 'Fall' and year = 2009 and
      course_id in (select course_id
                    from section
                    where semester = 'Spring' and year = 2008);
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">What happens behind the query</div><div class="two"><div><div class="flow-label">Outer: Fall 2009 courses</div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">105</span><span class="chip on">237</span><span class="chip">242</span><span class="chip">304</span><span class="chip">334</span><span class="chip">486</span><span class="chip">960</span></div></div><div><div class="flow-label">Subquery result: Spring 2008 courses</div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">158</span><span class="chip on">237</span><span class="chip">345</span><span class="chip">349</span><span class="chip">362</span><span class="chip">704</span><span class="chip">852</span><span class="chip">962</span><span class="chip">991</span></div></div></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">Each Fall 2009 course is looked up in the subquery result. Only <b>237</b> is found → <code>in</code> keeps it. The other 6 are <i>not</i> found → <code>not in</code> keeps those.</p></div>
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th></tr><tr><td>237</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
<p>Swap <code>in</code> for <code>not in</code> to get courses offered in Fall 2009 but <b>not</b> in Spring 2008:</p>
```

```sql
... and course_id not in (select course_id
                        from section
                        where semester = 'Spring' and year = 2008);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>course_id</th></tr><tr><td>105</td></tr><tr><td>242</td></tr><tr><td>304</td></tr><tr><td>334</td></tr><tr><td>486</td></tr><tr><td>960</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(6 rows)</div>
```

### ⚠️ Trap: `not in` when the subquery contains `null`

```{=html}
<p><i>Example:</i> Find faculty members who are <b>not</b> library members. In <code>members</code>, the <code>id</code> column holds faculty ids, and it is <code>null</code> for every student member.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: lis</div>
```

```sql
select faculty_fname, faculty_lname, id
from faculty
where id not in (select id from members);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>faculty_fname</th><th>faculty_lname</th><th>id</th></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(0 rows) · expected 1 row, got none</div>
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Why: evaluating <code>not in</code> for Pinki Mandal (id = FMCA05)</div><p style="margin:0 0 6px"><code>x not in (v1, v2, …)</code> means <code>x &lt;&gt; v1 <b>and</b> x &lt;&gt; v2 <b>and</b> …</code></p><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>comparison</th><th>result</th></tr><tr><td>'FMCA05' &lt;&gt; 'FCS01'</td><td>true</td></tr><tr><td>'FMCA05' &lt;&gt; 'FCS02'</td><td>true</td></tr><tr><td>… (each of the other faculty member ids)</td><td>true</td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>'FMCA05' &lt;&gt; <span class="nl">null</span> (a student member)</td><td><b>unknown</b></td></tr></table></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">true <b>and</b> true <b>and</b> … <b>and</b> unknown = <b>unknown</b>. <code>where</code> keeps only rows that are <b>true</b>, so Pinki is dropped. With even one <code>null</code> in the subquery, <code>not in</code> can never be true.</p></div>
<p><b>Fix 1</b>: remove nulls from the subquery. <b>Fix 2</b>: use <code>not exists</code>, which never compares against <code>null</code>.</p>
```

```sql
-- Fix 1
select faculty_fname, faculty_lname, id
from faculty
where id not in (select id from members where id is not null);

-- Fix 2
select faculty_fname, faculty_lname, id
from faculty f
where not exists (select * from members m where m.id = f.id);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>faculty_fname</th><th>faculty_lname</th><th>id</th></tr><tr><td>Pinki</td><td>Mandal</td><td>FMCA05</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row) · both fixes</div>
```

### Set Comparison: `some` and `all`

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Clause</th><th>True when</th><th>Logic</th></tr><tr><td><code>F &lt;comp&gt; some r</code></td><td>the comparison holds for <b>at least one</b> row of r</td><td>∃ t ∈ r : F &lt;comp&gt; t</td></tr><tr><td><code>F &lt;comp&gt; all r</code></td><td>the comparison holds for <b>every</b> row of r</td><td>∀ t ∈ r : F &lt;comp&gt; t</td></tr></table></div><p>&lt;comp&gt; can be <code>&lt;</code>, <code>&lt;=</code>, <code>&gt;</code>, <code>&gt;=</code>, <code>=</code>, <code>&lt;&gt;</code>. <code>any</code> is a synonym for <code>some</code>.</p>
<p><i>Example:</i> Find instructors who earn more than <b>some</b> / more than <b>all</b> Physics instructors. Physics has two instructors: Shuming (108011.81) and Voronina (121141.99).</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
select name, dept_name, salary
from instructor
where salary > some (select salary
                     from instructor
                     where dept_name = 'Physics');

-- replace some with all for the second query
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Salaries in descending order</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th><th>salary</th><th>&gt; some Physics</th><th>&gt; all Physics</th></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Wieland</td><td>Pol. Sci.</td><td>124651.41</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Voronina</td><td>Physics</td><td>121141.99</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Mird</td><td>Marketing</td><td>119921.41</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Sakurai</td><td>English</td><td>118143.98</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Bietzk</td><td>Cybernetics</td><td>117836.50</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Bondi</td><td>Comp. Sci.</td><td>115469.11</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Shuming</td><td>Physics</td><td>108011.81</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Lent</td><td>Mech. Eng.</td><td>107978.47</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Kenje</td><td>Marketing</td><td>106554.73</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>…</td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></table></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0"><code>&gt; some</code> = above the <b>smallest</b> Physics salary (108011.81) → 6 rows. <code>&gt; all</code> = above the <b>largest</b> Physics salary (121141.99) → only Wieland. Voronina is not greater than her own salary, so she fails <code>&gt; all</code>.</p></div>
<div class="two"><div><div class="flow-label">&gt; some</div><div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th><th>salary</th></tr><tr><td>Wieland</td><td>Pol. Sci.</td><td>124651.41</td></tr><tr><td>Voronina</td><td>Physics</td><td>121141.99</td></tr><tr><td>Mird</td><td>Marketing</td><td>119921.41</td></tr><tr><td>Sakurai</td><td>English</td><td>118143.98</td></tr><tr><td>Bietzk</td><td>Cybernetics</td><td>117836.50</td></tr><tr><td>Bondi</td><td>Comp. Sci.</td><td>115469.11</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(6 rows)</div></div><div><div class="flow-label">&gt; all</div><div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th><th>dept_name</th><th>salary</th></tr><tr><td>Wieland</td><td>Pol. Sci.</td><td>124651.41</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div></div></div>
```

#### Equivalences to remember

```{=html}
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>Expression</th><th>Same as</th><th>Why</th></tr><tr><td><code>= some</code></td><td><code>in</code></td><td>equal to at least one value</td></tr><tr><td><code>&lt;&gt; all</code></td><td><code>not in</code></td><td>different from every value</td></tr><tr><td><code>&gt; some</code></td><td><code>&gt; min(…)</code></td><td>beating the smallest is enough</td></tr><tr><td><code>&gt; all</code></td><td><code>&gt; max(…)</code></td><td>must beat the largest</td></tr><tr><td><code>&lt;&gt; some</code></td><td><b>not</b> the same as <code>not in</code></td><td>true if the value differs from <i>any one</i> value; with two different values in r it is almost always true</td></tr></table></div>
<p><b>Edge case:</b> if the subquery returns <b>no rows</b>, <code>&gt; all</code> is <b>true</b> for every row (nothing to fail against) and <code>&gt; some</code> is <b>false</b> (nothing to succeed against).</p>
```

### Test for Empty Relations: `exists` / `not exists`

```{=html}
<p><code>exists r</code> is true if r returns at least one row; <code>not exists r</code> is true if r is empty. The columns returned do not matter, so <code>select *</code> is normal here.</p><p>Usually the subquery is <b>correlated</b>: it refers to a column of the outer query (the <b>correlation name</b>), so it is re-evaluated <b>once for every outer row</b>.</p>
<p><i>Example:</i> Find teams that have <b>never lost a home match</b>.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: flis</div>
```

```sql
select t.name
from teams as t
where not exists (select *
                  from matches as m
                  where m.host_team_id = t.team_id
                        and m.host_team_score < m.guest_team_score);
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Subquery run once per team (t = current outer row)</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>take one team t</b></div><span>outer row</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>run subquery</b></div><span>home losses of t</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>empty?</b></div><span>not exists = true</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>keep t</b></div><span>else drop</span></div></div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>t.name</th><th>subquery result: home losses</th><th>result is</th><th>not exists</th></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Amigos</td><td>M0016 (1-2)</td><td>non-empty</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Thunder</td><td>M0002 (0-1)</td><td>non-empty</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Rainbow</td><td>M0003 (2-3), M0012 (1-2)</td><td>non-empty</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Black Eagles</td><td>M0004 (1-2), M0014 (1-2)</td><td>non-empty</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>All Stars</td><td>(empty)</td><td>empty</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span> kept</td></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Arawali</td><td>(empty)</td><td>empty</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span> kept</td></tr></table></div></div>
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th></tr><tr><td>All Stars</td></tr><tr><td>Arawali</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(2 rows)</div>
<p>Using <code>exists</code> instead gives the opposite question. <i>Example:</i> teams that <b>won at least one away match</b>:</p>
```

```sql
select t.name
from teams as t
where exists (select *
              from matches as m
              where m.guest_team_id = t.team_id
                    and m.guest_team_score > m.host_team_score);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th></tr><tr><td>Thunder</td></tr><tr><td>Rainbow</td></tr><tr><td>Black Eagles</td></tr><tr><td>All Stars</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(4 rows)</div>
<p><i>Example:</i> departments that have <b>no instructor</b>.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
select d.dept_name
from department as d
where not exists (select *
                  from instructor as i
                  where i.dept_name = d.dept_name);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th></tr><tr><td>Civil Eng.</td></tr><tr><td>History</td></tr><tr><td>Math</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(3 rows)</div>
```

### "For All" Queries with `not exists … except`

```{=html}
<p>SQL has no "for all" keyword. To find rows related to <b>every</b> item of a set, use: <i>X ⊇ Y</i> ⇔ <i>Y − X = ∅</i>, written as <code>not exists (Y except X)</code>.</p>
<p><i>Example:</i> Find teams that have played against <b>every other team</b> (home or away).</p><div class="ds">Dataset: flis</div>
```

```sql
select t.name
from teams as t
where not exists (
    -- Y: all other teams
    (select team_id from teams where team_id <> t.team_id)
    except
    -- X: teams t has played against
    (select guest_team_id from matches where host_team_id = t.team_id
     union
     select host_team_id from matches where guest_team_id = t.team_id)
);
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Y − X for each team</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>Y</b></div><span>every other team</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>X</b></div><span>teams t has played</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>Y except X</b></div><span>teams never played</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>empty?</b></div><span>keep t</span></div></div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt "><tr><th>t</th><th>Y</th><th>X (opponents)</th><th>Y − X</th><th>not exists</th></tr><tr class="hit"><td>Amigos (T0001)</td><td>T0002 – T0006</td><td>T0002, T0003, T0004, T0005, T0006</td><td>∅</td><td><span class="tick">✓</span> kept</td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Thunder (T0002)</td><td>5 teams</td><td>T0001, T0004, T0005, T0006</td><td>T0003</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Rainbow (T0003)</td><td>5 teams</td><td>T0001, T0004</td><td>T0002, T0005, T0006</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Black Eagles (T0004)</td><td>5 teams</td><td>T0001, T0002, T0003</td><td>T0005, T0006</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>All Stars (T0005)</td><td>5 teams</td><td>T0001, T0002</td><td>T0003, T0004, T0006</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr><tr class="miss"><td>Arawali (T0006)</td><td>5 teams</td><td>T0001, T0002</td><td>T0003, T0004, T0005</td><td><span class="cross">✗</span></td></tr></table></div></div>
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th></tr><tr><td>Amigos</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
```

### Test for Duplicates: `unique`

```{=html}
<p><code>unique (subquery)</code> is true if the subquery result has <b>no duplicate rows</b> (an empty result counts as unique). <i>Example:</i> teams that hosted <b>at most one</b> match.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: flis</div>
```

```sql
-- SQL standard (lecture syntax)
select t.name
from teams as t
where unique (select m.host_team_id
              from matches as m
              where m.host_team_id = t.team_id);
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output in PostgreSQL</div><pre>ERROR:  UNIQUE predicate is not yet implemented</pre><p>PostgreSQL does not support <code>unique</code>. Here every row of the subquery is the same <code>host_team_id</code>, so "no duplicates" means "at most one row". Rewrite it with a count:</p>
```

```sql
select t.name
from teams as t
where (select count(*)
       from matches as m
       where m.host_team_id = t.team_id) <= 1;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>name</th></tr><tr><td>All Stars</td></tr><tr><td>Arawali</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(2 rows)</div>
```

## Subqueries in the `from` Clause

```{=html}
<p>A subquery in <code>from</code> produces a temporary relation that the outer query uses like a table. This lets you filter on an aggregate with <code>where</code> instead of <code>having</code>.</p><p><i>Example:</i> Departments whose average salary is greater than 90000.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
select dept_name, avg_salary
from (select dept_name, round(avg(salary), 2) as avg_salary
      from instructor
      group by dept_name) as dept_avg
where avg_salary > 90000;
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">Two stages</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>inner query</b></div><span>one row per department (17 rows)</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>as dept_avg</b></div><span>name the result</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>outer where</b></div><span>keep avg_salary &gt; 90000 (6 rows)</span></div></div></div>
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th><th>avg_salary</th></tr><tr><td>Physics</td><td>114576.90</td></tr><tr><td>Finance</td><td>105311.38</td></tr><tr><td>Pol. Sci.</td><td>100053.07</td></tr><tr><td>Geology</td><td>99382.59</td></tr><tr><td>Comp. Sci.</td><td>98133.47</td></tr><tr><td>Cybernetics</td><td>96346.57</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(6 rows) · row order may vary; add order by avg_salary desc to fix it</div>
<p>Equivalent with <code>having</code>: <code>select dept_name, avg(salary) from instructor group by dept_name having avg(salary) &gt; 90000;</code></p>
```

### The `with` Clause

```{=html}
<p><code>with</code> defines a temporary, named relation that exists only for the query that follows. <i>Example:</i> the department with the maximum budget.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
with max_budget(value) as
    (select max(budget) from department)
select department.dept_name, department.budget
from department, max_budget
where department.budget = max_budget.value;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th><th>budget</th></tr><tr><td>Physics</td><td>942162.76</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(1 row)</div>
<p>Several <code>with</code> relations can be chained, each using the earlier ones. <i>Example:</i> departments whose total salary is greater than the average total salary of all departments (228235.85).</p>
<div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>dept_total</b></div><span>sum of salaries per dept</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>dept_total_avg</b></div><span>average of those sums</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>final select</b></div><span>departments above it</span></div></div>
```

```sql
with dept_total(dept_name, value) as
    (select dept_name, sum(salary)
     from instructor
     group by dept_name),
dept_total_avg(value) as
    (select avg(value) from dept_total)
select dept_name, dept_total.value
from dept_total, dept_total_avg
where dept_total.value > dept_total_avg.value;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th><th>value</th></tr><tr><td>Statistics</td><td>406772.65</td></tr><tr><td>Athletics</td><td>385490.99</td></tr><tr><td>Cybernetics</td><td>385386.27</td></tr><tr><td>Marketing</td><td>336389.75</td></tr><tr><td>Pol. Sci.</td><td>300159.22</td></tr><tr><td>Elec. Eng.</td><td>296650.96</td></tr><tr><td>English</td><td>288356.20</td></tr><tr><td>Physics</td><td>229153.80</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">(8 rows) · row order may vary</div>
<p>⚠️ Write <code>dept_total.value</code> in the select list, not just <code>value</code>. Both relations have a column called <code>value</code>, so PostgreSQL reports <code>column reference "value" is ambiguous</code>.</p>
```

## Subqueries in the `select` Clause

```{=html}
<p>A <b>scalar subquery</b> returns exactly one value and can be used wherever a single value is expected. <i>Example:</i> each department with its number of instructors.</p><div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
select dept_name,
       (select count(*)
        from instructor
        where department.dept_name = instructor.dept_name) as num_instructors
from department
order by dept_name;
```

```{=html}
<div class="out-label">Output</div><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>dept_name</th><th>num_instructors</th></tr><tr><td>Accounting</td><td>4</td></tr><tr><td>Astronomy</td><td>1</td></tr><tr><td>Athletics</td><td>5</td></tr><tr><td>Biology</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>Civil Eng.</td><td>0</td></tr></table></div><div class="rows-note">First 5 of 20 rows shown</div>
<p>Note <b>Civil Eng. → 0</b>: a scalar subquery that counts still returns one row. Compare with a join + <code>group by</code>, which would drop departments with no instructors.</p>
<p>⚠️ If the subquery returns <b>more than one row</b>, the query fails at runtime:</p>
```

```sql
select d.dept_name,
       (select i.name from instructor i where i.dept_name = d.dept_name)
from department d;
```

```{=html}
<pre>ERROR:  more than one row returned by a subquery used as an expression</pre>
```

## Modifying the Database

```{=html}
<div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>delete</b><span>remove rows</span></div><div class="box"><b>insert</b><span>add rows</span></div><div class="box"><b>update</b><span>change values</span></div></div>
<p>These statements change the dataset. Wrap them in <code>begin; … rollback;</code> while practising so your copy of the data is restored afterwards.</p>
```

### Deletion

```{=html}
<div class="ds">Dataset: university</div>
```

```sql
begin;
-- delete instructors in departments located in the Taylor building
delete from instructor
where dept_name in (select dept_name
                    from department
                    where building = 'Taylor');
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<pre>DELETE 7</pre>
<p><b>Tricky case:</b> delete instructors earning less than the average salary.</p>
```

```sql
begin;
delete from instructor
where salary < (select avg(salary) from instructor);
select count(*) from instructor;
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<div class="panel"><div class="panel-title">As rows are deleted, the average would change, so SQL works in two phases</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 1</b></div><span>compute avg once: 77600.19</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 1</b></div><span>mark rows below it: 23</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>phase 2</b></div><span>delete marked rows</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>result</b></div><span>50 → 27 instructors</span></div></div></div><pre>DELETE 23
 count
-------
    27</pre>
```

### Insertion

```sql
begin;
insert into course
values ('CS-999', 'Data Visualisation', 'Comp. Sci.', 3);

-- column list given: unlisted columns become null
insert into course (course_id, title)
values ('CS-998', 'Seminar');
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<p>The whole <code>select-from-where</code> of an <code>insert … select</code> is evaluated <b>before</b> any row is inserted; otherwise <code>insert into r select * from r</code> would never end.</p>
<p>⚠️ <b>Watch the primary key.</b> The lecture query below fails on the course dataset, because an instructor id already exists as a student id:</p>
```

```sql
insert into student
select id, name, dept_name, 0
from instructor;
```

```{=html}
<pre>ERROR:  duplicate key value violates unique constraint "student_pkey"
DETAIL:  Key (id)=(96895) already exists.</pre><p>The statement is atomic: none of the 50 rows are inserted.</p>
```

### Updates

```{=html}
<p>Give a 3% raise to salaries over 100000 and 5% to the rest. With two separate updates, <b>order matters</b>: running the 5% update first could push a salary over 100000 and it would then get the 3% raise as well. A <code>case</code> expression does it in one pass:</p>
```

```sql
begin;
update instructor
set salary = case
                 when salary <= 100000 then salary * 1.05
                 else salary * 1.03
             end;
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<pre>UPDATE 50</pre>
<p><b>Update with a scalar subquery:</b> recompute each student's total credits from passed courses.</p>
```

```sql
begin;
update student as s
set tot_cred = (select sum(c.credits)
                from takes as t, course as c
                where t.course_id = c.course_id
                      and t.id = s.id
                      and t.grade <> 'F'
                      and t.grade is not null);
rollback;
```

```{=html}
<pre>UPDATE 2000</pre><p>A student with no passed course would get <code>null</code> (sum of no rows). Use <code>coalesce(sum(c.credits), 0)</code> to store 0 instead.</p>
```
